sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: following distances, the move-over law, red-light penalties and courses, divided and undivided roadways, alleys and left turns
Look-alike numbers and rules from the pedestrian, emergency-vehicle and school-bus pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A02
The following distance behind an emergency fire department vehicle is 500 feet, while behind an emergency police vehicle it is 300 feet. [A02]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty three; confusable sec10-F27 versus sec10-F28.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A02
A red-light crash with life-threatening injuries carries up to $500 and three months of suspension, while a crash causing death carries up to $1,000 and six months. [A02]
Why it matters: group red-light penalties; difficulty three; confusable sec10-F17 versus sec10-F18.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A02
Traffic Survival School is ordered by MVD after a red-light conviction, and skipping it ends in an indefinite suspension. [A02]
Why it matters: group red-light penalties; difficulty two; confusable sec10-F19 versus sec10-F22.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A02
With an approaching emergency vehicle on an ordinary road you pull right and stop, while on a four-lane highway with two lanes in its direction you move to a lane not next to it. [A02]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty three; confusable sec10-F24 versus sec10-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A02
Paying a red-light fine is not a quiet way out: it is reported to MVD as a conviction and points go on the record. [A02]
Why it matters: group red-light penalties; difficulty two; confusable sec10-F21 versus sec10-F20.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
A red-light or other civil traffic citation may make you eligible for the Defensive Driving Program, and the options are explained in the papers that come with the citation. [A01]
Why it matters: group courses; difficulty three; prereq sec10-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A03
The move-over law is about driving past a vehicle that is already pulled over at the roadside with its flashing lights on, whatever kind of vehicle it is. [A03]
Why it matters: group move over; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F30.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A03
Under the move-over law you change one lane away, and only if that is unsafe or impossible do you slow down and use caution instead. [A03]
Why it matters: group move over; difficulty two; confusable sec10-F30 versus sec10-F31.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A03
Oncoming drivers may pass a loading school bus only on a roadway divided by a physical barrier; painted lines alone leave everyone required to stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty three; confusable sec10-F39 versus sec10-F40.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
A stopped school bus is released when it moves on or when both its stop-sign arm and flashing lights are put away. [A03]
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F37.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A01
Leaving an alley or driveway you stop before the sidewalk and then yield, while turning left you yield to oncoming vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians. [A01]
Why it matters: group yielding; difficulty two; confusable sec10-F09 versus sec10-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A01
A U-turn is legal unless a sign bans it, it cannot be made safely, or it would interfere with other traffic. [A01]
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]
